interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology revealed a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological stage pT2. A positive surgical margin was documented, which is an adverse finding. Countervailing factors include the absence of extraprostatic extension and no invasion of the seminal vesicles, as stated in the surgical pathology report: "There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; no lymph nodes were removed." Nodal status is uncertain as no nodes were removed, and "pNx is not pN0." The biopsy report is missing Gleason pattern and ISUP information. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding the true extent of disease. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 63.30 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 41.14–85.45 months; its coverage has not been validated.
